notes: Reached FR storefront via the Akamai interstitial proof-of-work solver (curl_cffi chrome-impersonation session, POST /_sec/verify?provider=interstitial), same method validated on sibling stores GB (SR90), DE (SR106) and ES (SR117); store 84009901, catalog 80209919, languageId -2. Checked: (1) the full mega-menu tree embedded as JSON in the homepage's serverApp-state (/api/storefront/1/stores/84009901/menu?language=fr-FR&clientId=web-zh&catalogId=80209919), (2) robots.txt (5840 bytes, no Claude/anthropic-ai-named disallow), (3) the site's own FR category sitemap (https://www.zarahome.com/8/info/sitemaps/sitemap-home-categories-zh-fr-0.xml.gz, 668 URLs, full-text scanned for 'nouveaut'/'meilleur'/'vente'/'solde'/'destock'/'bestsell'/'outlet'/'fin-de'/'liquidat'/'populaire'/'tendance' substrings). Found exactly one standalone New Arrivals-type page: the top-level nav item 'NOUVEAUTES' -> https://www.zarahome.com/fr/nouveautes-collection-n942, present as its own entry in the FR sitemap, categoryId 1020447643, seoId 942 -- the identical shared Inditex taxonomy node already confirmed for the same concept on sibling stores GB (/gb/new-in-collection-n942), DE (/de/neuheiten-kollektion-n942) and ES (/es/novedades-coleccion-n942), populated here with FR's own catalogue. A second internal menu entry also named 'NOUVEAUTES' (breadcrumb ENFANTS ET BEBES > NOUVEAUTES, menuEntryId 1020377506, keyword 'enfants', seoId 1094, content.type=grid, seoExtraInfo.irrelevant=true) resolves only to the Kids department's own landing page as an in-page celement widget, the same non-genuine pattern documented on GB/DE/ES for their Kids 'New In' entries -- not present as its own URL in the FR sitemap, so not emitted as its own row. Opened the genuine page directly: rendered <title> = 'Nouveautes | Zara Home France'; <meta name=description> = 'Decouvrez les dernieres nouveautes de la semaine chez Zara Home. Trouvez de l'inspiration et suivez les tendances pour meubler et decorer votre interieur avec style.' i.e. 'Discover the latest new arrivals of the week at Zara Home' -- self-describing as newly added products, not a themed campaign. Confirmed real filterable product grid via the underlying API response's own 'filters' object (live facets present). Read the exact server-side API the page itself calls: GET /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009901/80209919/category/1020447643/product?showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false&languageId=-2&appId=1 -> productIds array length = 466. Independently cross-checked by collecting every ccId across all 227 rendered gridElements blocks (some blocks bundling a Bundle+Product pair into one visual tile): unique ccId set size = 466, identical set membership to productIds (zero discrepancy either direction). sortedProductIds (narrower Product-kind-only subset) = 375, not used, consistent with prior sibling findings that the raw productIds/rendered-tile set is the reliable exact metric for this storefront (FR renders no plain 'N items/produits' text header anywhere in the grid, matching GB/DE/ES/UAE). Used 466 as qty. No genuine New Arrivals sub-structure exists as separate sitemap-listed URLs, so this is emitted as a single row. Fifth consecutive Zara Home country site (after UAE/GB/DE/ES) to show this exact single-genuine-New-Arrivals-PLP pattern.
